units.notes: Nothing was asked for this unit. The regulator's plant list dated 26 June 2026 shows Staudinger 4 as grid reserve, which is still operating in GEM terms, with 660 MW gross and 580 MW net, commissioned in 1977. I left the unit alone.

Status.note: A trade magazine reported on 5 May 2026 that the Regierungspräsidium Darmstadt, the state permit authority, issued a preliminary decision (Vorbescheid) for the planned block 8 at Staudinger. Uniper says the next step is to file a first partial permit in the third quarter of 2026 and a second one for construction and operation in the second quarter of 2027. A second news article confirms the preliminary decision at the end of April 2026. Uniper is actively seeking its permits, so the status moves from announced to pre-construction. Both articles rest on Uniper's own announcement, so I count them as one origin. The preliminary decision is not a full construction permit and no construction has started.

Capacity (MW).note: The trade magazine article of 5 May 2026 says block 8 is planned with an electric output of up to 890 MW. This matches the current value.

Equipment Manufacturer/Model.note: The article says the preliminary decision procedure was carried out together with the technology partner Siemens Energy. It does not name a turbine model and does not say outright that Siemens Energy supplies the turbine. So this is a likely maker only.

Start year.note: A trade magazine article from the time of Uniper's announcement says commissioning is aimed at the end of 2029. This matches the current value.

Latest Activity.note: A trade press article from 18 August 2026 says Uniper plans two hydrogen-ready gas plants, one of them at Staudinger, that could already take part in the first capacity tender. Uniper declined to give details of its bid. The award is not due before 3 November 2026.

Status Detail.value: Preliminary decision for the plant issued by the Regierungspräsidium Darmstadt at the end of April 2026. First partial permit to be filed in the third quarter of 2026. Gas and steam turbine plant, which is a combined cycle design.
Status Detail.note: The article calls the plant a gas and steam turbine plant. This settles the doubt in the old note: it is a combined cycle design, so the technology value stays as it is.

Turbine/Engine Technology.note: The article describes block 8 as a gas and steam turbine plant. That is a combined cycle plant.
